articleTitle: Research on Monitoring and Coal Volume Estimation Methods for Belt Conveyors
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: This paper proposes a computer vision monitoring method based on coal mine belt conveyors. A camera is installed above the belt conveyor to collect the image data of the belt surface, and the computer vision method is used to achieve the detection of the operating status of the belt conveyor and the estimation of the volume of coal transported. First, a motion detection method based on background subtraction is used to detect the pixel changes on the belt surface to determine the operating status of the belt conveyor. Then YOLOv8n network is used to detect the material area on the belt conveyor. Finally, the instantaneous coal volume is estimated based on the width occupied by the boundary of the material region. It is proved through experiments that the method proposed in this paper can effectively monitor the operating status of the belt conveyor and the material conveying status.

articleTitle: Research on Relation Extraction in the Field of Aviation Electrical Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: In order to reduce the troubleshooting time of aviation electrical maintenance and effectively utilize unstructured textual information related to electrical systems, we proposed an improved model for relationship extraction using CASREL. This model incorporates entity recognition and relationship extraction techniques to identify faults and extract relationships, aiming to enhance the efficiency of reading and searching through manuals and facilitate knowledge sharing among maintenance staff. For handling overlapping relationships among electrical fault entities, we adopted a cascaded binary labeling framework. To strengthen the model’s ability to capture local features, we employed BERT-wwm-ext as the encoder and introduced a self-attention module based on scaled dot product. Additionally, we enhanced the nonlinear capability and complex feature learning capability by replacing the single Linear layer in the annotator with a multi-layer perceptron. To evaluate the effectiveness of our improvements, we conducted several sets of comparative ablation experiments. The results demonstrate a 7.5% improvement in the F1 value of our improved model compared to the original model, achieving a value of to 96.7%. It provides a solid foundation for subsequent implementations of aviation electrical knowledge graph and intelligent fault diagnosis system.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Transformer with Sparse Attention for Gastrointestinal Disease Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) disease recognition is significant for early detection and effective treatment, leading to improved patient outcomes. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, particularly vision transformer, demonstrate their effectiveness in medical diagnosis. This paper adopts a novel approach, namely Bidirectional Transformer with Sparse Attention (BTSA) for GI disease recognition. The proposed model leverages the power of transformer architectures and incorporates sparse attention mechanisms to handle the diversity and complexity of GI diseases. By learning from large-scale datasets, BTSA can effectively identify patterns and anomalies associated with different GI diseases. The sparse attention mechanism boosts the representation learning on relevant regions and features, improving both performance and computational efficiency. Extensive experiments prove the outstanding performance of BTSA in GI disease recognition, surpassing existing models successfully. The proposed BTSA model holds significant potential to revolutionize the diagnosis and management of GI diseases, assisting healthcare professionals in making informed decisions and ultimately improving patient care. Further research and validation are required to explore the full capabilities and clinical utility of BTSA in real-world healthcare settings.

articleTitle: Research on Student Performance Prediction Model Based on Blended Learning Data
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: Abstract-Student performance prediction is a highly sought-after research direction in the field of education, and accurately predicting final exam scores is crucial for improving teaching quality. In this study, blended learning data from the “Fundamentals of Programming (C)” course at Qinghai University from 2016 to 2019 was used. By combining SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) oversampling and Bayesian optimization algorithm, four commonly used machine learning models were employed to evaluate students’ final performance based on process-oriented learning data. The experimental results showed that these four models achieved accuracy rates of 86%, 84%, 85%, and 86% in predicting students’ grade levels. Moreover, in predicting specific final exam scores, the root mean square errors of these models were 0.35, 0.28, 0.17, and 0.17, respectively. These findings indicate that these four models can provide accurate and effective references and guidance for students and teachers, further optimizing the teaching and learning process. By comprehensively analyzing students’ process-oriented learning data, we can reveal the patterns of their academic performance in the course and use them as a basis for predicting students’ grades.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection Method Based on RB-SMOTE and Double Attention
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of unbalanced traffic data collected in the real network environment and inaccurate feature representation of traditional machine learning methods, this paper proposes an intrusion detection method based on RBSMOTE and double Attention. Firstly, based on a refined Borderline-SMOTE method (RB-SMOTE), the intrusion data is oversampled to solve the problem of data imbalance, and the advantages of the convolutional network in image feature extraction are used to extract Convert one-dimensional flow data into grayscale images. Then, the low-dimensional features are dimensionally updated from the channel dimension and the spatial dimension through the dual-attention network to obtain a more accurate feature representation. Finally, the softmax classifier is used to classify and predict the traffic data. This method has been verified on the NSL-KDD dataset, and its accuracy rate reaches 99.24%, which is higher than other commonly used methods.

Author Keywords: the problems of unbalanced traffic data

articleTitle: Research on Stacked Model for Cluster CPU Utilization Prediction Based on Butterworth Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: Accurately estimating CPU and disk utilization in a cluster is crucial for avoiding failures and reducing unnecessary losses. Although there are many mathematical and machine learning methods that can roughly predict the future trends of time series data, these methods are not applicable to all data. Although deep learning algorithms have a wide range of applications, they lack interpretability. This paper proposes a stacked model based on Butterworth data filtering the STACK_XGBOOST model, which combines data filtering with statistical methods, machine learning algorithms, and deep learning methods. Firstly, the 4-sigma method is used to remove outliers in the data. Then, the Butterworth filter is used to smooth the trend of the time series data. Next, mathematical statistics, machine learning algorithms, and deep learning methods are used for prediction. Finally, XGBoost is chosen as the meta-model, and the prediction results of each baseline model are used as input to obtain the final prediction results, thereby improving the accuracy of resource utiliztaion prediction. Experimental data collected from the past 13 days of cluster CPU utilization is used for testing in a Computing Center. The experimental results show that compared to individual time series prediction algorithms, the STACK_XGBOOST model has lower average absolute error, higher prediction accuracy, and stronger interpretability.

articleTitle: A Survey of Evolutionary Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: Evolutionary algorithm is a kind of according to the selection and evolution of biological evolution model and the evolution of a kind of random search technology. Evolutionary algorithm is a blend of genetics, and cell biology evolution, therefore has a comparatively complete theoretical basis. Evolutionary algorithm has a good robustness, parallelism and flexible structure and so on. At present, widely used in path planning, feature selection, image processing, etc. This paper introduces the four parts, first is the basic theory of algorithm and the characteristics of the general framework, algorithm research, mathematical model and algorithm of improvement.

articleTitle: RFD:Detecting SAR Coastal Ship Targets Based On Reducing Feature Decay
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image has been widely used in the detection of ship target. Especially with the development of artificial intelligence, machine learing has been applied for ship detection in SAR images. However, it is hard to detect small scale ship in the SAR image using the current methods of SAR ship detection due to the image characteristics such as inshore complex background, geometric distortion, low pixel values, and limited useful information. In response to these problems, we propose a detection method based on feature reducing decay which could decrease the loss of effective information, i.e., reducing feature decay (RFD) module. First, one of the feature extraction models named RFD-ELAN model is suggested to reduce the loss of valuable information caused by multiple convolutions and activation functions. Then, the Refine-IoU loss function is used for loss calculation, which could provide a relatively accurate representation of the difference between prediction bounding box and ground truth bounding box. Finally, we utilize clustering analysis to improve the adaptability of anchor boxes and reduce redundancy in prediction areas. The experimental results show that the detection accuracy of the proposed algorithm has increased by 2.77% and 3.9% respectively, compared with the baseline for mAP_0.5:0.95 in the SIRSDD and HRSID coastal ship dataset. The experimental results show that the detection accuracy of the proposed algorithm is higher than that of baseline for both mAP_0.5:0.95 in the SIRSDD and HRSID coastal ship dataset, which improvement is 2.77% and 5.1% respectively.

articleTitle: Graph Structure-Based Implicit Risk Reasoning for Long-Tail Scenarios of Automated Driving
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: With the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology, autonomous vehicles (AVs) have entered the general public's view, however, the challenges brought by "long-tail" scenarios are still faced in the real driving process. Since long-tail scenarios rarely exist in the training dataset, the current data-driven autonomous driving system is hard to handle the implicit risk of these scenarios, which seriously affects the safety of driving. To alleviate this situation, A reasoning methodology is proposed to recognize implicit risk supporting making safety decisions in long-tail scenarios. The method firstly constructs the knowledge leading to long-tailed risks into a knowledge graph structure with spatial relations, and manages the knowledge graph based on GloVe (Global Vectors for Word Representation) word vector embedding technique with hash table structure. Following, by designing a real-time scenario topology graph generation model, this work computes the similarity between real-time topology graph and knowledge map through graph structure and spatial relationship, to obtain the probability of occurrence of long-tailed risk. Finally, the feasibility of the solution is verified in Carla simulation environment by a long-tail scenario example, which indicates the approach succeeds in identifying the implicit risk. This research provides a path for enhancing risk management and safety decision making in autonomous driving, especially in addressing the challenges of long-tail scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on Parameter Prediction of Heating System in a Middle School Based on Optimized Sample Features
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: In order to optimize the parameters of the secondary network process of the heating system, a data collection system for heating based on the Internet of Things was built in a middle school in Tianjin. After the system was built, heating season data from 2020, 2021, and 2022 was collected. After analysis, it was found that there were significant differences between the daily flow, supply and return water temperatures of the secondary network of the heating system and the curve obtained by the formula. Afterwards, the water temperature and daily flow of the three heating seasons were optimized in MATLAB by combining outdoor meteorological data. Multiple days and multiple meteorological factors were used as sample features, and a random forest was used to build a prediction model. The importance of sample features was highlighted using visualization tools, and they were screened. Then, according to the CS optimizttion, a BP neural network was established to predict the supply and return water temperatures and daily flow using the screened sample features. The results showed that in the random forest prediction model, the correlation coefficients (R2) of supply and return water temperatures and daily flow were improved from 0.46, 0.4, and 0.55 to 0.70, 0.69, and 0.64, respectively. In the BP neural network prediction model, the determination coefficients (R) of supply and return water temperatures and daily flow were 0.76, 0.83, and 0.91, respectively, indicating that this sample feature optimizttion method can effectively improve the prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: VRLVMix: Combating Noisy Labels with Sample Selection based on Loss Variation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: Since deep neural networks can fully fit all data, including noisy labels, that is, mislabeled data, this will be detrimental to the robustness and generalization ability of the network. To address this problem, existing methods usually use small loss tricks to select clean samples for training. However, sample selection using only small loss techniques cannot distinguish between large loss “hard” samples and noise samples. In this work, we analyze the reasons why clean samples are misidentified as noise samples and propose a balanced selection mechanism based on loss variation. This method sorts the amount of loss change, uses variance to count the rankings of multiple epochs to describe the stability of loss variation, and selects samples with stable loss as clean samples to reduce the misclassification of “hard” samples. At the same time, semantic clustering is used to assist resampling and reweighting, thereby alleviating the negative impact <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> of class imbalance on sample selection. We conduct comparative experiments and ablation experiments on synthetic noise datasets and real-world datasets such as CIFAR-10/100 and Clothing1M. Our VRLVMix has been shown to outperform numerous state-of-the-art methods, as evidenced by the experimental results. Moreover, it demonstrates the ability to extract clean samples even from large loss sample.

articleTitle: Ghost Detection Using Spatial Features-Intensity Fusion for Autonomous Mining Trucks
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: The multi-dust environment in open-pit mines presents a great challenge for the perception of autonomous mining trucks, leading to a large number of ghost detections (i.e., dust is detected as an obstacle), which seriously affects the production efficiency and increases the risk of accidents involving other traffic participants. To solve the ghost detection problem, this paper proposes a Spatial Features-Intensity Fusion method based on LiDAR point clouds collected from real mining areas. This method first constructs an offline data bank of obstacles and dust, in which the prior feature distributions of surface distance, angle, area, and reflected intensity of point clouds are analyzed. In the online classification pipeline, the grid clustering algorithm extracts point cloud clusters in a specific experimental scenario. Then the similarity between features of extracted point cloud clusters and prior feature distributions in the data bank is calculated using the Mahalanobis distance, which determines whether the current point cloud cluster is a ghost detection. The results show that for all detected point cloud clusters of the same category, the classification accuracy of the proposed method achieves 100% for obstacles and 96% for dust. Moreover, misjudging little dust as an obstacle will not lead to risks, and in most cases does not significantly affect the transportation efficiency of autonomous mining trucks. This method has the potential to help autonomous mining trucks eliminate interferences from adverse weather conditions such as dust, rain, snow, and fog, which is necessary for driving safety and efficient production in autonomous mining areas.

articleTitle: Ranking the Spreading Influence of Nodes in Complex Networks by Combining Local Average Weight and Average Normalized Link Entropy
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: Ranking the spreading influence of nodes is of great importance for controlling the spreading process on networks. Although a few measures are proposed for ranking nodes in weighted networks, it is still a challenge in accurately and efficiently ranking the spreading influence of nodes in weighted networks. In this paper, by utilizing both of the local and global topological structure information, a novel method is proposed. First, we define a local average weight (LAW) to describe the local topological structure information of nodes. Second, partly based on the link diversity, we define an average normalized link entropy (ANLE) to describe the global topological structure information of nodes. Further, by combining the LAW and ANLE, we propose a novel ranking measure termed as LAW-ANLE (LA) centrality. The proposed LA is verified by extensive experiments on a series of networks, and the results show that the LA is feasible and effective in accurately ranking the spreading influence of nodes.

articleTitle: MSDU: Multi-step Delayed Communication for Efficient Distributed Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: Distributed deep learning has emerged as the principal training paradigm in recent years. However, significant communication overhead often leads to a severe degradation of performance in data parallelism, which limits the scalability of distributed training. To address this problem, this paper introduce a novel MSDU (Multi-Step Delayed Update) method. MSDU mitigates the negative impact of communication overhead on training efficiency by introducing a delay in the parameter aggregation process. Which allowing for overlap between computation and communication. As a result, MSDU can improve the performance of distributed deep learning, particularly in scenarios with limited communication bandwidth, such as PCIe-based communication. Experimental results demonstrate that employing the MSDU method in data parallelism can significantly reduce training time by up to 45.7%, with only a limited loss of model accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhanced YOLOv7-Based Construction Site Environmental Detection Method
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: This paper proposes an enhanced approach utilizing the YOLOv7 model for automated construction site environment detection and management. The method leverages high-resolution surveillance cameras and computer vision techniques to achieve this goal. The proposed method starts with data collection of the construction site environment. Then produce accurate bounding boxes. These bounding boxes serve as input to an improved YOLOv7 network model, enabling feature extraction and generating high-scoring feature maps with associated weights. Utilizing these weights, image segmentation is performed to obtain the desired detection heads. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the method in identifying and annotating various environmental features within the construction site, leading to significant improvements in detection accuracy. Compared to similar techniques, this method offers faster detection speed, higher accuracy, and reduced error rates. The proposed construction site environment detection method provides an efficient and automated solution for on-site management in the construction industry, with practical applications and value.

articleTitle: Blockchain Based Auditable Access Control for Ship Furl Consumption Manage
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: Presently, the shipping industry is grappling with challenges pertaining to the security and auditability of ship fuel consumption data. To address this issue, this study introduces a novel auditable access control solution based on blockchain technology. The core objective is to ensure the safeguarding of ship fuel consumption data’s integrity and security, while concurrently enabling authorized stakeholders to access and manage this data in alignment with regulations.The research establishes a consortium blockchain platform involving multiple parties, encompassing shipping companies and regulatory bodies. To ensure that only duly authenticated users gain access to fuel consumption data, the study devises smart contracts and employs attribute-based access control policies. Rigorous performance tests validate the system’s throughput capabilities under high-concurrency scenarios, thereby underscoring its viability in practical deployments. This groundbreaking solution introduces fresh perspectives to the domain of ship fuel consumption management. By preserving data confidentiality and integrity, and meticulously documenting and auditing access procedures, the solution effectively mitigates the risks of data leakage and unauthorized alterations. This holds paramount significance, not only for enhancing the economic and environmental endeavors of the shipping industry but also for offering a practical avenue to enhance data security and auditability within distributed applications.

articleTitle: Location Prediction of PTI Station Based on Machine Learning and GIS
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: Periodical technical inspection of vehicles plays a vital role in ensuring road safety. The selection of suitable locations for vehicle inspection stations, responsible for conducting the regular inspection, has long been a matter of significant concern for companies. This paper proposes a method for selecting optimal locations of vehicle inspection stations based on machine learning and real-time GIS electronic map data. Focusing on Beijing’s vehicle inspection station as a case study, this study establishes an evaluation model that encompasses factors like competitive relationships, business ecology, and population number indexes. Utilizing machine learning algorithms including Gradient Boosting DeciSion Trees (GBDT), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), this paper analyzes the unique environmental characteristics of the vehicle inspection station at chosen addresses. The results indicate that the GBDT algorithm is most suitable for station location prediction, yielding accurate results.

articleTitle: Named Entity Recognition Method based on Bert-Bilstm-Attention-CRF for Education field
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: With the rapid development of the new generation of information technology, the educational information system has accumulated a large amount of educational data information, which makes learners have low cognitive efficiency, difficulty concentrating, and eventually deviate from learning goals and fail to complete specific learning tasks. This paper proposes a named entity recognition method in the education field combined with Bert-BiLSTM-Attention-CRE to improve learners’ learning efficiency. Firstly, BERT language model is used to extract text features to obtain the word granularity vector matrix; Then use Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) to extract the word-to-word relationship between the input statements and the context; Thirdly, Attention mechanism is introduced to better utilize local contextual clues by assigning different weights to the text feature vectors, and strengthen the correlation between current information and context information; Finally uses the Conditional Random Field (CRF) model to extract the globally optimal output label sequence according to the dependency between labels; and the named entity of the education field is obtained in the end. The experimental results show that the Precision, Recall and F1 value of the model are 82.25%, 79.73%, 80.39% respectively, the overall recognition performance is high, and the effect is better than that of BiLSTM-CRF, CNN-BiLSTMCRF, HIDCNN, BERT-BiLSTM-CRF.

articleTitle: Health Monitoring System Based on The Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: In order to meet the health monitoring needs of social smart medical care, this paper designs and implements a multi-scenario health monitoring system based on Internet of Things (IoT), namely local health monitoring based on Bouffalo Lab BL706 microcontroller and remote health monitoring based on mobile-Internet. It can realize undisturbed monitoring of the health status of users’ vital signs, including heart rate, body temperature and heart rhythm. The experimental results show that, the accuracy error of the heart rate measurement of this system is 2.1 times per minute, the accuracy error of temperature measurement is 0.13 °C, while the sensitivity of arrhythmia detection verified in the public database is 97.33% and the specificity is 95.22%. This paper combines users’ requirement for disturbance-free, multi-functional and multi-scenario health vital signs monitoring, which has great application value and market prospects in the field of remote health monitoring.

articleTitle: Short-term Subway Passenger Flow Prediction based on GCN-LSTM-MHA
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: The short-term prediction of subway passenger flow is of great reference value for the operation and management of the subway system. To improve the accuracy of the prediction results, this paper designs a combined model based on Graph Convolutional Neural Network and Long Short-Term Memory Network with Multi-Head Attention mechanism. Moreover, the Tree-Structured Parzen Estimator is used to optimize the relatively important hyperparameters in the model. Experimental results demonstrate that the GCN-LSTM-MHA model effectively captures the spatiotemporal correlation of subway passenger flow data and outperforms other baseline models in terms of prediction accuracy.
